data.text:
F32 is at records 152 and 153, and it is **detected rather than fully prevented**. That
distinction is the whole of this note, because a round that reported it as closed would be
making the same kind of claim this ticket has already produced four findings about.

## What is closed, verified

Planting the ordinary Supabase RPC pattern in `public`, a `security definer` function
selecting from `public.tenants`, makes the suite exit 1 and name it: "2 routines in schema
public can be executed by a role a browser request is bound to. Schema public is served by
the Data API, so each of them is a POST /rpc/<name> endpoint reachable with the anon key,
and a `security definer` one runs as its owner". Part 6 raises on the same condition at
migration time, so a migration fails when it runs and not only when the suite next runs.

## What is not closed, verified

A function created after the fix is still callable by `anon`. Measured on the reset
database: the postgres-grantor default ACL for functions is now `{postgres=X,service_role=X}`,
so the revoke did what it says, and yet a new function is born `{=X/postgres,postgres=X,
service_role=X}` and `has_function_privilege('anon', ...)` is **true**, and `anon` read both
tenants' names through it.

The reason is that PostgreSQL grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every routine as a baseline, and a
`pg_default_acl` entry is merged into that baseline by adding to it rather than by replacing
it. So `alter default privileges ... revoke` cannot reach the PUBLIC grant on a function at
all. It is not that the fix was written badly; it is that this mechanism cannot do this job.

Two further limits stand: the `supabase_admin` grantor's entry still grants `anon=X` and this
role cannot touch it, refused 42501, exactly as F19 found for tables; and revoking on
functions from `public` as well does not help, measured, because the built-in default is
reapplied to each new routine.

## Where that leaves the exposure, stated as a bound rather than as a closure

The pull request that adds the first function to `public` fails the suite inside itself, and
its migration raises when it applies. So the window is a branch, not production, and no
function exists in `public` today. That is a real bound and it is not prevention.

**The only complete prevention is an event trigger, which part 6 declines.** The round did not
reverse that decision, which is right: it was taken at a gate and reversing it is a gate's
call. But the reason part 6 gives for declining is now known to be false. It says a relation
added later is unreachable until somebody grants it, which is true of a relation and false of
a function, because a function is born reachable through PUBLIC and nobody grants anything.
So the decision should be retaken rather than inherited, with the true reason in front of
whoever takes it.

## The pattern this makes five of

F19 was `relkind = 'r'` in the tenancy and privilege guards. F29 was `relkind = 'r'` again in
the four guards a previous round had not widened. F30 was `relacl` where the question was
effective privilege. F32 is `on tables` where the exposed class is tables, views, sequences
and functions, and `config.toml` says so in as many words. Each fix answered the question in
front of it, and the next reviewer found the quarter of the sentence it had not answered.
F33, the sequence quarter, is open and is one statement away on this round's own mechanism.

## Found and not fixed

- Part 8 omits `seen.refuse_erasure_registry_mutation()` from its own revoke list, and
  `seen.touch_updated_at()` from part 1 keeps the PUBLIC default. Both are trigger functions
  that answer 0A000 when called by name, and PostgREST does not serve `seen`, so nothing
  crosses. Left to F38, which names it.
- `seen.current_tenant()` carries a redundant PUBLIC grant beside the three explicit ones.
- **The suite has no guard for schema `seen` at all.** Every helper asks about `public` only,
  so a later migration putting a `security definer` function in `seen` and exposing that schema
  in `config.toml` would meet nothing. That is not any current finding and is worth one.

F33 to F38 remain open.
